newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila files suit against Security Bank.
newsitem.headline: Manila files suit against Security Bank.

text.p: The Philippine Commission on Good Government (PCGG) has filed a civil suit against Security Bank Corp to recover 210 million pesos in deposits and to put another $16 million in an escrow account, the bank said on Thursday.

"(However) the bank ... is of the opinion that the case has no basis and will not prosper in court, and that liability or loss, if any, arising therefrom will not have a material effect on its financial condition," assistant corporate secretary Lourdes Crisostomo told the Philippine Stock Exchange.

The PCGG, which is the custodian of sequestered assets of former strongman Ferdinand Marcos and his business associates, said the 210 million peso deposit was made by former employees of the bank by way of inward remittances set out in spurious telexes.

Security Bank said it had already remitted 1.09 billion pesos to the government as part of its withdrawal of sequestered deposits. The inclusion of the 210 million pesos as part of sequestered assets is still being contested.

The PCGG also said the $16 million which it had helped Security Bank withdrew from a Zurich bank should be put in an escrow account since it is part of its recovery of ill-gotten wealth. The bank disagrees.
PCGG puts sequestered assets in escrow accounts until it has determined who the real owners are.
